senses.gloss:
Yayāti is mentioned twice in the Rigveda,^1 once as an ancient
sacrificer, and once as Nahuṣya, ‘descendant of Nahuṣa,’
apparently a king. There is no trace whatever of his connexion
with Pūru, as in the Epic,^2 the tradition of which must be
deemed to be inaccurate.
1) i. 31, 17; x. 63, 1.
2) Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the
Rigveda, 3, 147; Muir, Sanskrit Texts
12, 232.

Yāyāvara^1 denotes a person of no fixed abode in the Yajur-
veda Saṃhitās.^2
1) Literally, ‘wandering about,’ from
the intensive of yā, ‘to go.’
2) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 2, 1, 7;
Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xix. 12.
